intro.title: Explore Expiatorio Park
intro.entityLead: Welcome to Expiatorio Park, widely recognized as the central Parque Expiatorio. Located in the heart of Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico, this destination serves as a primary public landmark and hub for travelers visiting the region.
intro.nearbyText: When visiting Expiatorio Park, visitors can easily explore surrounding historical landmarks and points of interest, including Templo Expiatorio and the MUSA (Museum of the Arts, University of Guadalajara).
intro.description: Expiatorio Park (Parque Expiatorio) is located in the Col Americana neighborhood of Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico, adjacent to the magnificent Templo Expiatorio. It is a beautiful urban square that perfectly combines solemn religious faith with a strong local street life, making it an excellent place for tourists and local families to relax and enjoy authentic street food.

visitGuide.title: Visiting Tips
items: The park is open all day, daytime visits are recommended
Enjoy the green spaces and walking paths
Great for family outings and recreational activities
Explore the nearby Col Americana neighborhood

alsoKnownAs.title: Core Highlights
items: Neo-Gothic Landmark: Adjacent to Mexico's most magnificent neo-Gothic church, extremely stunning when illuminated at night.
Family Friendly: A warm and peaceful atmosphere with green spaces and walkways for citizens to relax, where children often play.
Night Food Market: In the evening, the square transforms into a famous local night food market, a mecca for tasting affordable authentic snacks.
Art District: Located in the artistic Col Americana neighborhood, surrounded by cafes and art venues.

route.title: Tour Route
route.overview: The ideal route to explore Expiatorio Park and experience the square's tranquility and vibrant life:
steps: 16:00: Arrive at the square, visit the stained glass windows inside the Templo Expiatorio, and wait for the twelve apostles statues on the clock tower to strike the hour at 18:00.

18:30: As night falls, the landscape lights on the church's outer wall light up. At this time, food stalls in the square begin to open. You can buy roasted corn or desserts and sit on the square benches to experience the local lifestyle.
19:30: Enjoy spontaneous local community activities in the square, such as open-air Salsa dancing lessons or family interactions.

20:30: After the tour, take a short walk to see the night view of the exterior of the Museum of the Arts of the University of Guadalajara (MUSA), or find a boutique cafe to rest in the surrounding Col Americana neighborhood.
supplements: Cash Preparation: Please prepare some small denomination peso cash, as food stalls and vendors in the square usually only accept cash.
Safety Tips: Although located in a good area with relatively good security, the square is crowded at night, so please keep an eye on your phone and wallet.
Weather Advice: Guadalajara's rainy season (May-October) mostly features afternoon or evening showers, please bring an umbrella.

sections.title: Historical Significance
sections.content: Expiatorio Park is a beautiful urban park in the Col Americana neighborhood of Guadalajara. The park offers green spaces and walking paths, making it an ideal place for relaxation and exercise.

sections.title: Cultural Landscape
sections.content: The park is adjacent to the magnificent Neo-Gothic Templo Expiatorio and surrounded by artistic buildings. It's an excellent place to experience Mexican urban life and street food, full of tranquility and vitality.

sections.title: Visiting Experience
sections.content: Visiting Expiatorio Park is a relaxing experience. You can walk in the green spaces, enjoy the natural scenery, feel the warm atmosphere of the park, and taste authentic food at night.

transport.title: Getting to Expiatorio Park
transport.airportDesc: Nearest airport: Guadalajara International Airport (GDL). Take a taxi or ride-hailing service to the Col Americana neighborhood.
transport.selfDriveDesc: Paid public parking is available right by the plaza, including an underground garage, though spaces fill up in the evening.
transport.busDesc: Several city bus routes serve the area (e.g. Ruta 622); you can also take the light rail (Mi Macro) to Juárez station and walk from there.
transport.intercityDesc: Very convenient if you are staying in Col Americana or the historic centre. Guadalajara Cathedral is about 1.4 km away (a 20-minute walk), making a pleasant combined walking route.
transport.cyclingDesc: Taxi/ride-hailing (Uber/DiDi) is the most recommended and safe transportation method.
transport.tipsDesc: Public transport or taxi are both fine; if driving, there are paid public parking lots nearby.

faq.title: Expiatorio Park (Guadalajara) - FAQ
faq.subtitle: Frequently asked questions about this iconic park in Guadalajara.

items.a: Expiatorio Park is located in the Col Americana neighborhood of Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico (postal code 44160).

items.q: Is there parking near Expiatorio Park?
items.a: Yes. Paid public parking is available around the park and Templo Expiatorio, including an underground garage right beside the square, plus metered street spaces. It gets busy in the evening, so arrive early and confirm rates on site.

items.q: Is Expiatorio Park free to visit?
items.a: Yes, Expiatorio Park is a public space and is free to visit year-round.

items.q: What are the opening hours of Expiatorio Park?
items.a: As a public open space, Expiatorio Park is accessible throughout the day; the night-market food stalls usually operate from evening until late at night.

items.q: What is the relationship between Expiatorio Park and Templo Expiatorio?
items.a: Expiatorio Park is the public square and gardens in front of Templo Expiatorio, the famous Neo-Gothic basilica adjacent to the park.

items.q: What can visitors explore near Expiatorio Park?
items.a: Visitors can easily explore surrounding landmarks and points of interest, including Templo Expiatorio and the MUSA (Museum of the Arts, University of Guadalajara).

items.q: How do I get to Expiatorio Park?
items.a: Expiatorio Park is in central Guadalajara and is reachable by bus, light rail (Mi Macro), taxi, or rideshare, with paid public parking available nearby.

aboutExpiatorio.title: Templo Expiatorio del Santísimo Sacramento: An Icon of Guadalajara

sections.title: History of the Expiatorio
sections.description: The history of the Templo Expiatorio dates back to the 19th century. Under the direction of Archbishop Pedro Loza y Pardavé, the project by prominent Italian architect Adamo Boari was selected. Construction began in 1897 and was not completed until 1972, taking 75 years due to the Mexican Revolution and economic crises.

sections.title: A Neo-Gothic Masterpiece
sections.description: The temple is a magnificent example of Neo-Gothic style, built mainly with carved stone. A particularly striking feature is its German-made clock with a musical carillon; every day at 9 a.m., 12 p.m., and 6 p.m., figures of the twelve apostles emerge. It is considered a masterpiece of Neo-Gothic architecture in Mexico.

sections.title: A Religious and Gastronomic Gathering
sections.description: The Expiatorio offers more than a spiritual experience; its esplanade is a vibrant place full of entertainment and delicious food options. You can enjoy pastries, elotes, tacos, and more. A few steps away, you can also explore the Museum of the Arts (MUSA).

sections.title: Why is it called Expiatorio?
sections.description: Although its official name is the Basilica of the Blessed Sacrament, it was given the name 'Expiatorio' in 1906 for ceremonies of expiation. It is said that if you visit the Pearl of the West and do not stop by the Expiatorio, it is as if you were never here.

stories.title: Tales & Legends: The Memory of the Expiatorio
stories.intro: Beyond the dates and architects recorded in history books, this old basilica lives on in the memories and evening conversations of several generations of Guadalajara locals. Below are stories and folklore widely shared around the city - they belong to oral tradition and urban memory rather than strict historical records, which makes them all the more endearing.

items.heading: The chime of the Twelve Apostles
items.text: The clock mechanism in the tower was built by a German workshop, and every day at 9:00, 12:00 and 18:00 the statues of the twelve apostles 'walk' across the top of the tower. Older locals love to wait in the square for this moment; it is said that a young couple who manage to count all twelve apostles together will be blessed with a long-lasting bond. Even today many families keep this as a regular part of their evening stroll.

items.heading: A church that took over half a century to build
items.text: From the foundation stone in 1897 to its formal completion in 1972, the works spanned nearly four generations and survived several interruptions without ever being abandoned. People in the old town like to say the church was not so much 'raised' as 'saved up' by generations of stonemasons - which is exactly why it is so deeply treasured today.

items.heading: Why it is called the 'Expiatorio'
items.text: Its official name is the Basílica del Santísimo Sacramento, but it gradually became known as the Expiatorio (the Expiatory) around 1906. As the elders tell it, people came not only to pray but also to leave a burden behind, walking out again with a calmer heart - as if completing an inner settlement.

items.heading: Fountains, pigeons and evenings in the square
items.text: Locals say you can tell a city truly treats its square as a 'living room' when neighbours are still happy to sit on the benches after dinner. Expiatorio Plaza is exactly such a living room: children chase pigeons, young people play guitars, and the glowing stalls of grilled corn (elote) and street snacks turn it into a moving portrait of daily life in Guadalajara.

stories.note: Note: these texts combine public sources with local oral traditions and are offered as cultural interpretation. Individual details may differ slightly between references and the memories of older generations.

services.title: Visitor Services & Facilities Nearby
services.subtitle: Neutral, type-based information on the everyday services you may need around the square
services.neutralNote: As a non-profit educational site we only describe types of facilities and general ways to find them - we do not recommend any specific business. Availability varies between blocks, so always check on site or with official sources.

items.name: Public restrooms (WC)
items.desc: A limited number of public restrooms is available around the square and the church. Many street-front restaurants, malls and service venues also provide customer restrooms - it is fine to ask politely whether they are open to the public.
tips: Look for facilities marked 'Sanitarios' or 'Baños'
Lines are common during the busy evening hours

items.name: Parking
items.desc: Paid public parking is available right by the Expiatorio square and Templo Expiatorio, including underground spaces (estacionamiento subterráneo); metered on-street parking (parquímetro) is also common in Colonia Americana. Spots near the core fill up at night - arrive early or use public transport.
tips: Prefer lots marked 'Estacionamiento público'
Check metered hours and rules to avoid fines
Expect tight parking on weekends and evenings

items.name: Dining
items.desc: Around the square you will find Mexican street food (grilled elote, tacos, street desserts), casual snack bars, cafés and ice-cream shops - from eat-on-the-go stalls to places where you can sit down.
tips: Food stalls facing the square open mostly in the evening
For seated meals, browse nearby streets for cafés and restaurants
Keep small change handy for stall purchases

items.name: Lodging
items.desc: Within easy walking distance you can choose among hostels, boutique hotels, business and family-oriented lodgings; rates generally rise the closer you get to the centre.
tips: Book ahead for weekends and festive seasons
Filter for 'breakfast included' or 'near transit' if useful
For large luggage, prefer lodgings with a lift

items.name: Shops & convenience stores
items.desc: Convenience stores, supermarkets, bakeries and souvenir shops are a few minutes' walk away, covering water, snacks, common medicines and gifts.
tips: Stores usually post clear prices; compare freely
Stock up on water and sunscreen before you start
Compare a couple of shops before buying souvenirs

items.name: Fuel & EV charging
items.desc: The historic core itself has few fuel stations. For driving visitors, stations are typically 5–15 minutes away along main roads, and some also offer electric-vehicle chargers.
tips: Check your fuel or battery before heading out
EV chargers are usually app-based; install the common payment apps
Large supermarket car parks often include charging bays

items.name: Pharmacies & cash
items.desc: Chain and neighbourhood pharmacies, bank branches and ATMs are scattered around the district, covering minor ailments and cash needs on foot.
tips: Prefer ATMs inside bank branches
Carry a little small-denomination cash for stalls
Ask your lodging front desk for the nearest pharmacy if needed

items.name: Accessibility & special needs
items.desc: The square is level with gentle ramps and many benches, comfortable for wheelchairs and strollers. The church's main steps are steep; guests with mobility needs can use side entrances and ask staff for guidance.
tips: Visit in the morning or after lunch when it is calmer
With a stroller, avoid the crowded evening stalls
Do not hesitate to ask on-site staff for assistance

itinerary.title: Recommended Standard Itineraries
itinerary.subtitle: A half-day and a full-day plan - choose by the time you have, or mix and match.
itinerary.note: Tip: the church's opening hours can change with religious services; check on-site or official notices. The apostle chime and the illuminated facade are best seen around sunset.

plans.name: Half-Day Highlights
plans.summary: Ideal for a first visit on a tight schedule, focused on the square and the church exterior.

steps.title: Arrival & first impression
steps.text: Walk the perimeter of the square and enjoy the full silhouette of the neo-Gothic spires and facade.

steps.title: Wait for the chime
steps.text: If timing allows, take a bench and wait for the 9:00 / 12:00 / 18:00 procession of the twelve apostles.

steps.title: Stroll the square
steps.text: Follow the shaded paths, watch family life unfold, and rest on a bench by the fountain.

steps.title: Street snack finale
steps.text: Grab a local treat from a stall as the lights come up and the square fills with evening life.

plans.name: Full-Day Immersion
plans.summary: For travellers who want a slower pace and the surrounding neighbourhoods too.

steps.title: Morning · church & old streets
steps.text: Start inside the church with its stained glass, then wander the historic blocks around the square.

steps.title: Afternoon · museum & café
steps.text: Walk to a nearby art museum and cultural site, then rest at a neighbourhood café.

steps.title: Evening · square life
steps.text: Return for the apostle chime and the illuminated facade - the square becomes the city's living room.

steps.title: Night · street food
steps.text: Close the day with grilled elote or a local snack from the evening stalls.

audience.title: Routes Tailored by Traveller Type
audience.subtitle: Three targeted plans for families, photography and nature lovers, and low-mobility visitors.
audience.note: All three routes stay around the square and its walkable surroundings, and can be freely combined with the itineraries above.

routes.meta: Suggested time: afternoon to evening · about 2–3 hours
routes.desc: Relaxed and playful: treat the open green square as a playground and the church as a giant storybook.
points: The apostle chime is the moment children love most
Picnics and kids' play are part of daily life here
Sharing a grilled elote makes a memorable family break

routes.meta: Suggested time: early morning / dusk · about 2–4 hours
routes.desc: Chasing light and composition: quiet mornings, warm evenings, and a dramatic tower facade in the blue hour.
points: Side light about one hour after sunrise suits the facade
Claim your spot before sunset to catch the lights turning on
A 24–70mm lens covers both wide views and details

routes.desc: Slow and gentle: level paths, gentle ramps and benches as your resting posts - sit and watch the world go by.
points: Enter via the main gentle ramps to save energy
Benches and shade are frequent for short breaks
Finish near the square to avoid long transfers

responsibility.title: Education & Visitor Responsibility
responsibility.subtitle: The more you know, the more responsibly you enjoy your visit.
responsibility.note: Mindful tourism itself is the best way to protect and respect this century-old landmark.

items.title: Heritage & public facilities
items.text: Do not climb sculptures, fountains or railings, and never carve on the stonework. Use bins or take your litter with you.

items.title: Etiquette in a place of worship
items.text: The church is still in active use: stay quiet, dress respectfully, avoid noise during services, and check whether flash photography is allowed before taking pictures inside.

items.title: Leave-no-trace & friendly visits
items.text: Street performers and vendors are part of the city's vitality - a polite interaction is all it takes. If feeding the square's pigeons, do so sparingly and keep the ground clean.

items.title: Safety of belongings & transport
items.text: In the busy evening crowds, keep an eye on your phone, camera and wallet; use licensed public transport or book rides through official platforms.

nearby.title: Things to Do & Where to Eat Nearby
nearby.subtitle: Within easy walking distance of the basilica: day spots, night food and landmarks worth combining.
nearby.note: As a non-profit educational site we describe only types of places, never specific businesses; always check current names and hours on site.

cards.title: By day · cafés & pastry shops
cards.text: Along the historic blocks you will find pastry shops (postrería), cafés and Italian-style casual dining for an afternoon break, while chain pharmacies and convenience stores make it easy to stock up nearby.

cards.title: By night · Guadalajara street food
cards.text: After dark the food stalls around the plaza open up: grilled corn (elote), esquites, tacos, plus local icons such as tortas ahogadas, a cool tejuino and regional desserts - authentic flavours without needing to pick any single vendor.

cards.title: Nearby · museum & old town
cards.text: The MUSA (University of Guadalajara Arts Museum) is a few minutes' walk away; from the Expiatorio to the Cathedral is about 1.4 km (a 20-minute walk, or 5 minutes by car), ideal for linking the basilica with the old-town plazas in one day.
